title: Green wins Hockenheim Race 1 as Audi's title fight goes to the last race
dek: Jamie Green won Race 1 at Hockenheim for Audi from third on the grid, 3.9 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller, who passed pole-sitter Glock late, and the title was left open for Sunday.

chapters.title: Four Audis chase the title in the finale
text: The DTM season ended at the Hockenheimring on 14–15 October, on the same track that had opened the year in May, when Lucas Auer won the Saturday race and Jamie Green the Sunday one. Two races remained, and the championship was still open to six drivers, four of them in Audis. Mattias Ekström of Abt Sportsline led with 172 points, 21 ahead of Rosberg's René Rast, a rookie in his first full season, while Green and Mike Rockenfeller were further back. The previous round at the Red Bull Ring had gone one each to Ekström, who won Race 1, and Rast, who took Race 2.

Each race ran for 55 minutes plus one lap and included a mandatory pit stop, so strategy mattered as much as pace. A second pressure came from the stewards: warnings collected during the season were converted into grid penalties for the next race, which meant that an incident on Saturday could cost a title contender places on Sunday. DTM chairman Gerhard Berger said he hoped the Audi drivers would be allowed to race each other freely, adding that he would not necessarily bet on Ekström if they were.

Rockenfeller was quickest in Friday practice. The paddock also had an eye on the future: two Super GT cars, a Lexus LC 500 driven by Heikki Kovalainen and a Nissan GT-R driven by Ronnie Quintarelli, ran demonstration laps at race speed on all three days, a preview of the common technical rules the DTM and Super GT planned to share from 2019.

chapters.title: BMW hits back with a front-row lock-out
text: Timo Glock put his BMW M4 on pole in the Saturday session with a 1:30.648. Maxime Martin, in the second BMW from the Team RBM garage, was 0.037 seconds behind, so BMW held the whole front row. The Audis of Green and Rast took the second row, 0.122 and 0.155 seconds off the pace, and the three fastest qualifiers collected 3, 2 and 1 championship points. Glock said the car had been in the right window on his lap after a difficult Friday, and expected Audi to be stronger in the race.

For the title fight the interesting part was behind the leaders. Ekström, the points leader, managed only tenth, 0.308 seconds slower than Glock, which cooled hopes of clinching early. Rockenfeller was seventh and Marco Wittmann, the reigning champion, eighth, with Nico Müller's Abt Audi ninth between them and Ekström. Mercedes found little to celebrate: Edoardo Mortara was fifth and Robert Wickens sixth, while Gary Paffett qualified 11th and Paul di Resta 13th. Auer was 15th, and Maro Engel 17th ahead of only Loïc Duval's Phoenix Audi.

Green, the best-placed Audi driver in third, played down the result, saying that qualifying was not Audi's strength and that he would simply do his own race. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz said the grid was not what his team had hoped for and that more had been possible.

chapters.title: Green takes the lead from Glock and is warned for it
text: Glock kept the lead off the line and Green passed Martin, who had made a poor getaway, to move into second. On lap six Green went for the lead: Glock had to take a wide line over the kerbs and turned sharply back in front of the Audi, and Green was through soon afterwards, at the hairpin. The stewards gave Green a warning for forcing Glock off the track, and because it was his fifth of the season he would drop ten places on the grid for Sunday.
Green said the penalty was annoying, as he had not been flat out and had not meant to push the BMW wide. Glock said Green simply had the speed early on and that he could not hold him.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller stays out and finds fresh tyres
text: Green held the lead through the mandatory stops and stayed in front after his own, but the stop windows opened the door for a different strategy. Rockenfeller, who had qualified seventh, ran longer than most of the leaders, looked after his tyres and attacked on the fresh set once he came in, working his way up through the field to second place.

Glock, who had been running behind Green, watched the stops on the big screens in the circuit and saw the Audi rejoin around Martin; he knew then that Rockenfeller would be a threat to him. Ekström, meanwhile, received a warning for forcing Engel's car off the track, his third of the year, so he too would start five places back on Sunday.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller takes second from Glock as Ekström fails to score
text: Green crossed the line 3.939 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller, who passed Glock for second in the closing stages, and Glock finished third, 5.666 seconds behind the winner. Rockenfeller also set the fastest lap, a 1:32.819 on lap 34. Glock said he had been unsure whether the last lap had come, but that third was a good result and that Audi, with the best car, would have one of its drivers on top of the final standings.

Martin was fourth, 10.448 seconds back, and Mortara fifth as the best Mercedes. Rast was sixth from fourth on the grid, then Wickens, Auer, Paffett and Bruno Spengler completed the top ten, which meant four Mercedes scored. Ekström took 11th and no points, followed by Müller, Wittmann in 13th from eighth on the grid, di Resta, Tom Blomqvist, Engel, Augusto Farfus and Duval.

Audi had secured the drivers' title for the marque, but with four of its drivers still in contention it was not yet decided who would take it. Ekström still led with 172 points, but his advantage over Green had shrunk to nine, with Rast on 159 and Rockenfeller 20 behind the leader. Mercedes, with Auer out of it too, had left the title picture for good.

facts.t: Audi one-two for Green and Rockenfeller
facts.v: Green won by 3.939 seconds from Rockenfeller, who climbed from seventh on the grid to second on a longer first stint.
